set.scene:
The Kobayashi IV made Bleakhold Station on one good thruster, and the clamps took her with a groan. The raider cutter that jumped you on the lane is scrap now, drifting somewhere behind you, but her last volley opened the port hull plating and cooked a power relay, and the damage board shows more amber than green. The dockmaster, Oren Halvard, logged your scorched hull without a word and waved off the first night's berth fee.

You are in the galley now, with the hatch sealed. Your ribs ache where the harness caught you, blood has dried along your forearm from the relay fire, and your hands have not quite stopped shaking. The stores locker is close to bare, because the fight and the long burn here ate most of what you carried. Beyond the hatch, Bleakhold's market hums through the deck.

set.scene:
The docks of Hollow Spire run dry and dim at this hour, ration notices pasted over older ration notices. Tamsin Okoro's stall sits at the far end under its one lamp, her ledger open in front of her as thick as a door. She looks up when your shadow crosses the page, and nods you to the stool she keeps for people she does not mind.

"Three freighters overdue this month, all on the Bleakhold run," Tamsin says, turning the ledger so you can read the column. Her finger stops on the last name. "The Lark's Tithe. My sister's boy, Joss, crewed her." Two stalls down, Idris Vane the water-seller is counting ration chits into a tin and pretending not to listen. Traders drift past in ones and twos, and none of them meets your eye for long.

set.scene:
The Kobayashi IV sits against Hollow Spire's docking collar with her reactor idling, and you are alone in the cockpit with the pre-flight board. Tamsin Okoro's last message is still on the comm panel: the Bleakhold run is the one the raiders keep hitting, four days out along the marked lane, and Bleakhold Station is where the missing freighters were bound.

Under it she has added a second line: a set of coordinates with no name against them, a debris drift well off the charts where a salvager swears he saw a cutter lying dark. The lockers behind your seat have not been gone through since the last port, and the lamps of the Spire's docks slide slowly across the viewport as the ship turns on her clamp.

set.scene:
Hollow Spire's docks are loud tonight, for once: word has run ahead of you that the Bleakhold clerk talked. You set the sealed ledger on Tamsin Okoro's counter and she reads the seal twice. It is the harbourmaster's own. Corvin Hale of Bleakhold Station has been buying the freighter schedules and sending the cutters after them, and the proof of it lies under her lamp.

Warden Ysolde Marr of the lane authority stands at the end of the counter in her grey sash, hands folded, waiting to hear it from you. Tamsin has not let go of your sleeve since you came in. "All these months," she says quietly, "and you kept coming back to this stall."

set.scene:
Bleakhold Station's records office is a long, cold room of filing drums, and at this hour it holds one clerk. Devan Roe has the Hollow Spire freight schedules open on his desk and a second, smaller ledger half hidden under his sleeve. When you put the copied sailing times in front of him, the same times the raiders struck, the colour leaves his face.

"I only pass them along," Roe says, too fast. "A man collects them at the cargo lock, every tenth day. I never asked who he works for." His hand is still on the second ledger. Behind him the drum that holds the outbound manifests stands unlocked, and through the office window you can see the cargo lock he means, empty for now.

set.scene:
Two days past the last charted marker, the debris drift closes around the Kobayashi IV like a slow tide: hull plates, ice, the ribs of ships older than the lanes. You have been feeling your way toward the coordinates Tamsin Okoro passed on, where a salvager swore he saw a raider cutter lying dark. Nothing out here has a name on any chart you own.

Ahead, half buried in the drift, hangs the wreck of a relay station, its dish torn and its docking ring still slowly turning. Beyond it the debris thickens into a tumbling wall with one narrow gap. Your scanner paints a faint, regular heat trace somewhere on the far side.

set.scene:
Half a day out of Bleakhold Station on the marked lane, the Kobayashi IV's proximity alarm goes off like a dropped tray. A cutter has come up out of the sensor shadow of a dead freighter, close enough to read the name burned into her prow: the Cinder Wren. Her gun ports are open.

"Kobayashi IV, cut your drive and stand by to be boarded," a voice says on the open channel, bored, as if reading from a card. A warning shot crosses your bow and scatters into the dark. The dead freighter's hulk drifts between you, trailing a slow cloud of spilled cargo, and the lane behind you is empty all the way back to Bleakhold.
